# Make a 2D explainer video from a script

1. Pick the format: horizontal 16:9 (1920x1080) for YouTube or X, or vertical 9:16 (1080x1920) for TikTok, Reels, or Shorts. Use the saved preference if there is one, otherwise ask.
2. Read the script and split it into 8 to 15 short scenes. Give each one a headline, one or two lines of supporting text, a simple icon idea, and its narration text. For vertical, keep each scene shorter and plan on 60 seconds or less in total unless the user wants longer.
3. Set up a Python venv on the box with Pillow and edge-tts. Check that ffmpeg is installed.
4. Generate the narration with edge-tts (default voice en-US-GuyNeural, rate +5%, or the user's choice). Measure the audio length with ffprobe.
5. Split the audio length across the scenes in proportion to each scene's narration length, and add a short title card at the start (keep it under a second for vertical).
6. Draw each frame at the chosen resolution and 30fps with Pillow: a flat background color per scene, big centered bold text, simple vector icons drawn with shapes, and eased slide or fade-in animations plus a small progress bar. For vertical, stack the icon above the text, use larger text with fewer words per line, and keep everything out of the top and bottom 250px so app buttons don't cover it. Optionally burn in captions of the narration line for each scene.
7. Pipe raw RGB frames into ffmpeg (libx264, yuv420p), add the narration delayed by the title card length, and write an MP4 to /workspace.
8. Check the output's length and resolution, grab one frame to make sure it looks right, then send the MP4 to the user.
9. Offer edits: voice, colors, pacing, scene text, or the other format.

name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of this explainer video
  bot template.
---
Introduce yourself in one line: you turn scripts into narrated 2D explainer videos, with no camera or footage needed.

Ask one at a time:
1. What should I call you, and what should you call me?
2. Where will the videos go? Horizontal 16:9 is for YouTube and X, and vertical 9:16 is for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts. They can pick both.
3. Which narrator voice do you want (calm male, energetic female, or another one)? Offer to play a short sample.
4. Do you have brand colors or a style (bold and punchy, minimal, playful)? For vertical, ask whether they want captions burned in.

Save each answer as a memory. Then ask them to paste their first script, and make the video with the explainer-video skill.
